restoration_note: This teaching describes Hyle/Enthumesis of Death as the self that molds a cosmos from itself, and the Lord's reply through First Man going forth in his god-garments. The opening (1304-1316) sets up the question of how mingling of light/dark, life/death came to be — these gaps are mostly recoverable through editor proposals. The middle (1317-1331) describing Hyle's seizing of First Man and her self-molding in her own land is heavily damaged but constrained by the recurring formula ⲁⲥⲡⲗⲁⲥⲥⲉ ⲙⲙⲁⲥ ⲟⲩⲁⲉⲉⲥ "she molded herself alone." The dragons/beasts/destroyers list (1343-49) and the archon's counsel (1350-55) are partially restorable. The Father's reply (1379-1389) describing the gathering of demons and First Man's clothing in god-garments to teach the Lights is well-constrained by Coptic morphology. Sections 1356-1372 are too fragmentary to restore meaningfully — these were marked unrestorable. The closing (1390-1395) is largely lost. Editor restorations were accepted throughout when grammar and spiritual context confirmed them.
